propositions.text: This is an application for judicial review of a RAD decision dated April 8, 2019.
propositions.quote: This is an application for judicial review of a Refugee Appeal Division [RAD] decision, dated April 8, 2019

propositions.text: The RAD decision concluded the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee under section 96 IRPA nor a person in need of protection under section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: that concluded that the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA], nor a person in need of protection under section 97 of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is a judicial review of a RAD decision denying the Applicant refugee status and protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: The RAD confirmed the RPD's findings, especially that the Applicant had a viable Internal Flight Alternative in Islamabad, which was determinative.
propositions.quote: The RAD confirmed the findings of the Refugee Protection Division [RPD], in particular that the Applicant had a viable Internal Flight Alternative [IFA] in Islamabad (Pakistan), a finding that the RAD identified as determinative.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirmed the RPD's finding that the Applicant had a viable Internal Flight Alternative in Islamabad, which was determinative.

propositions.text: The Applicant argues the RAD's discussion on viable IFA was speculative about ongoing persecution threat.
propositions.quote: the Applicant argues that the RAD’s discussion as to the availability of a viable IFA was: (i) speculative as to the ongoing threat of persecution

propositions.text: The Applicant argues the RAD's discussion was incomplete, failing to assess the full range of factors under the second prong of the IFA test.
propositions.quote: and (ii) incomplete as it failed to assess the full range of factors under the second prong of the applicable test for an IFA.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the RAD's IFA discussion was speculative and incomplete regarding the second prong of the IFA test.

propositions.text: The RAD's decision was not unreasonable and the application for judicial review is dismissed.
propositions.quote: I conclude that the RAD’s decision was not unreasonable. I, therefore, dismiss the application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RAD decision was reasonable and dismisses the judicial review application.

propositions.text: The Applicant is a Pakistani citizen and drugstore owner in Sahiwal District, Punjab province.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Pakistan and the owner of a drugstore in the Sahiwal District. Sahiwal is located in the Punjab province of Pakistan

propositions.text: The Applicant is a trained pharmacy technician licensed to sell drugs and narcotics and supplied free contraceptives to a nearby doctor.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a trained pharmacy technician with a licence to sell drugs and narcotics. In addition to his regular business operations, the Applicant supplied free contraceptives to a nearby doctor.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant is a Pakistani citizen, drugstore owner, licensed pharmacy technician, and supplied free contraceptives to a doctor.

propositions.text: On August 15, 2016, unknown gang members threatened to kill the Applicant and family after he refused to supply bulk prescription medications.
propositions.quote: On August 15, 2016, a gang of unknown individuals came to the Applicant’s drugstore looking for prescription medications in bulk quantity. One of the individuals threatened to kill him and his family after the Applicant refused to supply them with the medicine.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant states unknown gang members threatened to kill him and family after he refused to supply bulk medications in August 2016.

propositions.text: On September 9, 2016, the same gang kidnapped, tortured, threatened, and beat the Applicant demanding medications; he escaped and reported to police.
propositions.quote: On September 9, 2016, the Applicant was the victim of a kidnapping incident...they tortured, threatened, and beat him...The Applicant was able to break away from the gang. He subsequently lodged a police report about the kidnapping incident.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant recounts a September 2016 kidnapping, torture, and threats by the gang, followed by escape and police report.

propositions.text: On September 10 and 15, 2016, religious leaders and Taliban members threatened the Applicant to close his drugstore and kill him and family.
propositions.quote: On September 10, 2016, the Applicant was threatened by a religious leader and certain members of the Taliban...On September 15, 2016, the Applicant was again threatened by another local religious leader and persons associated with the Taliban...they threatened to kill him and his immediate family.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant states he was threatened twice in September 2016 by religious leaders and Taliban to close his drugstore and kill him and family.

propositions.text: After threats, the Applicant closed his drugstore on September 16, 2016, and police refused to investigate after his request on September 18, 2016.
propositions.quote: On September 16, 2016, he closed his drugstore. On September 18, 2016, the Applicant contacted the local police to conduct an investigation but they apparently refused to do so.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant closed his drugstore after threats and police refused to investigate his complaint.

propositions.text: The Applicant moved with family to Karachi, received threatening calls on his business number, confirming fear of persecution, then left Pakistan for Canada on October 20, 2016.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, along with his family, moved to Karachi...the Applicant received threatening phone calls...To the Applicant, these phone calls confirmed his fear of persecution...The Applicant then left his home country for Canada on October 20, 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant moved to Karachi, received threatening calls, feared persecution, and left Pakistan for Canada in October 2016.

propositions.text: On November 30, 2016, the Applicant claimed refugee status, recounting threats and phone calls; a friend’s affidavit said unknown persons searched for him in Sahiwal in January 2017.
propositions.quote: On November 30, 2016, the Applicant claimed refugee status...According to an affidavit from the Applicant’s friend, unknown persons came to the village of Sahiwal searching for the Applicant on January 7, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant claimed refugee status in November 2016, recounting threats and a friend’s affidavit about persons searching for him in January 2017.

propositions.text: The refugee claim was transferred to the RPD, which held a hearing on June 15, 2017, and rejected the claim on June 30, 2017.
propositions.quote: His claim for refugee protection was transferred to the RPD. The RPD held a hearing on June 15, 2017, and rejected his claim on June 30, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD held a hearing in June 2017 and rejected the Applicant’s refugee claim.

propositions.text: Although the decision under review is the RAD’s, the RPD decision is set out in detail for context.
propositions.quote: Although the decision before me on review is that of the RAD, I think it is important in this case to also set out in some detail the decision of the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains it will detail the RPD decision despite reviewing the RAD decision.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Applicant’s credibility determinative, noting omissions, contradictions, vagueness, evasiveness, and unsuccessful explanations.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the Applicant’s credibility was determinative in the case; in particular, the RPD found that there were omissions and contradictions in the Applicant’s testimony as compared with his BOC, that his testimony was vague and evasive, and that he unsuccessfully attempted to explain the inconsistencies that were identified by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Applicant’s credibility determinative, citing omissions, contradictions, and evasiveness.

propositions.text: The RPD did not believe the Applicant was threatened as claimed and found he failed to prove risk of danger under subsection 97(1) IRPA in other Pakistan areas.
propositions.quote: the RPD did not believe that the Applicant was threatened by those he claims...or that those incidents actually took place...the Applicant had failed to meet his burden to demonstrate...that he would be personally subjected to the danger or the risk provided for in subsection 97(1) of the IRPA in other areas of Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD disbelieved the Applicant’s threats and found he failed to prove risk of danger under IRPA subsection 97(1).

propositions.text: Even if the Applicant was assaulted and threatened, the RPD found a viable IFA in Islamabad because the risk activity ceased with drugstore closure and no evidence of pursuit there.
propositions.quote: even if it had accepted that the Applicant had been assaulted and threatened...the Applicant nonetheless had a viable IFA in Islamabad...the activity that placed him at risk no longer exists...The Applicant has not demonstrated that his assailants would still have an interest in pursuing him...

propositions.text: The RPD found no evidence the Applicant would have difficulty travelling to or settling in Islamabad, noting his education, business success, and prior travel to Karachi.
propositions.quote: there is no evidence to suggest the Applicant would have difficulty travelling to Islamabad or settling down in that city in a reasonable manner. He is a successful, university-educated businessman who...had travelled to Karachi and started to earn his livelihood.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found a viable IFA in Islamabad since risk ceased and the Applicant could settle there easily.

propositions.text: The Applicant appealed the RPD decision to the RAD.
propositions.quote: The Applicant then filed an appeal from the RPD decision before the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant appealed the RPD decision to the RAD.

propositions.text: In his RAD appeal memorandum, the Applicant argued RPD erred in credibility and viable IFA findings, without new evidence or hearing request.
propositions.quote: In his memorandum on appeal to the RAD, the Applicant argued...that the RPD erred in its credibility finding...and that it also erred in the determination of a viable IFA. The Applicant did not present any new evidence, nor did he request a hearing before the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argued RPD erred on credibility and IFA but presented no new evidence or hearing request to RAD.

propositions.text: The Applicant suggested the viable IFA determination was made in a factual vacuum or false premise and that assailants could track him, without elaboration.
propositions.quote: the Applicant suggested only that the determination of a viable IFA was made in a factual vacuum, or was at least based upon a false premise, and that the Applicant provided evidence that his assailants were willing and able to track him down, without elaborating any further.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argued the IFA finding was made in a factual vacuum or false premise and assailants could track him, without details.

propositions.text: The RAD found the only determinative issue was the RPD’s IFA evaluation and dismissed the appeal, deeming credibility issues unnecessary to discuss.
propositions.quote: the only determinative issue was whether the RPD had erred in its evaluation of the IFA, and thus it was unnecessary to discuss the issues pertaining to the credibility of the Applicant. The RAD concluded that the RPD had adequately addressed that issue, and thus dismissed the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the IFA evaluation determinative, dismissed the appeal, and did not discuss credibility issues.

propositions.text: Whether the RAD committed a reviewable error in finding Islamabad offers a viable IFA.
propositions.quote: The only issue argued before me by the Applicant was whether the RAD committed a reviewable error in finding that Islamabad offers a viable IFA.

propositions.text: Applicant did not raise issue of RAD not ruling on RPD credibility finding.
propositions.quote: The Applicant did not raise the issue of the RAD not ruling on the credibility finding of the RPD.

propositions.text: RAD found discussion of RPD credibility unnecessary given its IFA viability finding.
propositions.quote: the RAD decision, which made it clear that, given its finding on the viability of the IFA, a discussion of the RPD’s credibility finding was not necessary.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the issue is whether RAD erred in finding Islamabad a viable IFA; applicant did not raise credibility issue; RAD found credibility discussion unnecessary.

propositions.text: Suggests RAD should address RPD credibility findings in future to avoid incomplete IFA analyses.
propositions.quote: in the future, in similar circumstances, the RAD may wish to address the credibility findings of the RPD, so as to avoid a situation where an IFA analysis is found by this Court to be unreasonable, and necessarily determinative solely on account of the lack of any analysis on credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court suggests RAD should address RPD credibility findings in future to avoid incomplete IFA analyses.

propositions.text: Vavilov sets presumption of reasonableness standard for administrative decisions, rebuttable by clear legislative intent or certain legal questions.
propositions.quote: In Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov], the Supreme Court set out a revised framework for determining the applicable standard of review for administrative decisions. The starting point is a presumption that a standard of reasonableness applies (Vavilov at para 23). This presumption can be rebutted in the presence of (1) a clear legislative intention to prescribe a different standard of review, or (2) the types of questions in which the rule of law requires the application of the standard of correctness

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Vavilov's framework presuming reasonableness standard unless rebutted by legislative intent or certain legal questions.

propositions.text: Applicant argues correctness standard applies because RAD violated natural justice and misapplied IFA test, raising central legal questions.
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that the impugned decision should be reviewed on the correctness standard because the RAD decision violates the principles of natural justice and does not adhere to the proper test for the determination of whether a viable IFA exists. In essence, the Applicant argues that the RAD conducted a speculative and incomplete analysis of his persecution claims concerning Islamabad that raises “general questions of law of central importance to the legal system as a whole”

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues correctness standard applies due to RAD's natural justice violation and improper IFA test application raising central legal questions.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD identified and followed appropriate test for viable IFA review.
propositions.quote: First, I find that the RAD did identify and follow the appropriate test in its review and determination with respect to a viable IFA.

propositions.text: Issues do not engage questions of central importance to legal system, but specific to Applicant.
propositions.quote: These are issues that do not engage with questions of central importance to the legal system, as the decision involves specific issues that most directly affected the Applicant.

propositions.text: No procedural fairness breach by RAD found.
propositions.quote: I am not convinced that there was any lack of procedural fairness attributable to the RAD.

propositions.text: Issue of IFA availability arises within RAD's delegated authority and is reviewed on reasonableness standard per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: this issue must be examined according to a reasonableness standard (Vavilov at paras 73-143).

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD applied correct test, no procedural fairness breach, and IFA issue is within RAD's authority reviewed for reasonableness.

propositions.text: IFA concept is essential to refugee system and ensures international refugee law backs national protection when inadequate.
propositions.quote: The question of whether an IFA exists is an essential component of the refugee system. The IFA concept flows from the definition of convention refugee and helps ensure that international refugee law serves as a backup to the national protection when such protection is inadequate

paragraphs.summary: Court states IFA concept is essential to refugee system, backing national protection when inadequate.

propositions.text: IFA concept ensures persecuted individuals seek protection within their country before international refugee system.
propositions.quote: the IFA concept helps ensure that persecuted individuals first approach their own country before seeking protection through the international refugee system

paragraphs.summary: Court explains IFA concept ensures persecuted seek protection within their country before international system.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant safe in Islamabad with no evidence of persecution agents pursuing him and ability to earn a living.
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the Applicant’s safety would be assured in Islamabad and that it would not be unreasonable for him to seek refuge there. In particular, the RAD concluded that there was no evidence that the alleged agents of persecution would pursue him in Islamabad , and that the Applicant could earn a living there as a businessperson.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed RPD’s conclusion that IFA was available to Applicant.
propositions.quote: On the basis of these factors, the RAD confirmed the RPD’s conclusion that an IFA was available to the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Applicant safe in Islamabad with no persecution risk and confirmed RPD's IFA conclusion.

propositions.text: Two-prong IFA test requires no serious persecution possibility and unreasonableness of seeking refuge in proposed IFA.
propositions.quote: this Court established a two-prong test to be applied in determining whether there is an IFA. Under the two-prong IFA test, it is required that: there is no serious possibility of the individual being persecuted in the IFA area (on the balance of probabilities); and conditions in the proposed IFA must be such that it would not be unreasonable in all the circumstances for an individual to seek refuge there

propositions.text: Both prongs must be satisfied for IFA finding; ensures compliance with international norms.
propositions.quote: Both prongs must be satisfied for a finding that the claimant has an IFA. This two-prong test ensures that Canada complies with international norms regarding IFAs

paragraphs.summary: Court states two-prong IFA test requires no serious persecution risk and unreasonableness test; both must be met for IFA.

propositions.text: Both prongs must be satisfied for IFA finding; ensures compliance with international norms.
propositions.quote: Both prongs must be satisfied for a finding that the claimant has an IFA. This two-prong test ensures that Canada complies with international norms regarding IFAs

paragraphs.summary: Court reiterates both prongs must be satisfied for IFA finding to comply with international norms.

propositions.text: Gallo Farias checklist clarifies IFA availability criteria including notice, two-step test, burden of proof, and reasonableness.
propositions.quote: Mister Justice Kelen provided a “checklist of legal criteria” that further clarifies this Court’s case law on the availability of an IFA: 1. If IFA will be an issue, the Refugee Board must give notice to the refugee claimant prior to the hearing ... 2. There is a disjunctive two-step test for determining that there is not an IFA ... 3. The applicant bears the burden of proof ... 4. The threshold is high for what makes an IFA unreasonable ... 5. The IFA must be realistically accessible ... 6. The fact that the refugee claimant has no friends or relatives in the proposed IFA does not make the proposed IFA unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court cites Gallo Farias checklist clarifying IFA criteria: notice, two-step test, burden, reasonableness, accessibility, and social ties.

propositions.text: Applicant submits RAD erred on both prongs of Rasaratnam-Thirunavukkarasu IFA test.
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the RAD committed errors in respect of both prongs of the Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits RAD erred on both prongs of the IFA test.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD's finding of no ongoing persecution risk conflicts with finding of viable IFA, alleging speculation.
propositions.quote: Applicant submits that the RAD committed an error when it determined that the agents of persecution are no longer interested in harming the Applicant, and yet also determined that there existed a viable IFA. There is an inconsistency, argues the Applicant, in the analysis as the RAD only speculated as to whether the threat continued to exist; the Applicant argues that one cannot speculate as to the existence of such a risk and then find that an available IFA exists.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD's no risk finding conflicts with viable IFA finding, alleging speculation and inconsistency.

propositions.text: Court rejects Applicant's argument; RAD concluded no risk of persecution or threat to life on return to Pakistan.
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Applicant’s argument. The RAD clearly, at the outset, analyzed the determination of risk and concluded that no such risk of persecution or threat to life continued to exist in the event the Applicant was to return to Pakistan .

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects Applicant's argument, finding RAD concluded no persecution risk on return to Pakistan.

propositions.text: RAD assumed risk continued for limited purpose of IFA review, stating even if assault and threat occurred, IFA would still exist.
propositions.quote: the RAD stated: “even if the panel had believed that the claimant had been assaulted and threatened in the manner alleged, which is not the case, it would still have rejected this refugee claim because it would have assessed that the claimant would have had an internal flight alternative (IFA) in his country, in particular in the capital city Islamabad.”

paragraphs.summary: RAD assumed risk continued for IFA review, stating even if assault occurred, IFA would still exist.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD did not speculate but assumed risk for IFA analysis, no inconsistency in IFA analysis.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RAD did not speculate, but only assumed, for the purpose of determining the existence of a viable IFA, that the risk continued to exist. I see nothing wrong with that approach, as it did not result, as is suggested by the Applicant, in an inconsistency in the IFA analysis by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD assumed risk for IFA analysis without speculation or inconsistency.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD's finding of Islamabad as IFA was a 'knee jerk' reaction without analysis.
propositions.quote: The crux of the Applicant’s argument is that the finding that Islamabad offered an IFA was but a “knee jerk” reaction, unsupported by any analysis as to its viability.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD's Islamabad IFA finding was a 'knee jerk' reaction lacking analysis.

propositions.text: Applicant had full opportunity to challenge Islamabad as IFA per Gallo Farias.
propositions.quote: in accordance with Gallo Farias (at para 34), the Applicant was given a full opportunity to challenge the suitability of Islamabad as an IFA.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant had full opportunity to challenge Islamabad as IFA.

propositions.text: Audio shows RPD identified Islamabad as acceptable IFA location without persecution risk.
propositions.quote: From the audio recording of the Applicant’s hearing before the RPD, it is clear that the RPD first identified Islamabad as an acceptable IFA location, where the Applicant would not be exposed to a risk of persecution

paragraphs.summary: Audio shows RPD identified Islamabad as acceptable IFA location without persecution risk.

propositions.text: RPD asked Applicant about living in Islamabad; Applicant said scared in Karachi but did not specifically address Islamabad safety, claimed countrywide threat.
propositions.quote: During the interview, the RPD member asked the Applicant why he left to go to Karachi , and whether he could live elsewhere in Pakistan such as Islamabad . The Applicant responded that he tried to resettle in Karachi but that he was scared that the persecutors would kill him. The Applicant did not specifically respond as to whether he could or could not live in Islamabad , but did claim that he would not be safe anywhere in Pakistan due to the agents of persecution’s countrywide network.

paragraphs.summary: RPD asked Applicant about Islamabad; Applicant expressed fear in Karachi but did not address Islamabad safety, claimed countrywide threat.

propositions.text: Threatening calls and friend's affidavit show continued risk of persecution even in Islamabad
propositions.quote: the threatening telephone calls received by the Applicant while he was living in Karachi , as well as his friend’s affidavit confirming that the assailants were still returning to the Applicant’s business in Sahiwal, demonstrate the continued nature of his risk of persecution, even in Islamabad .

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues threatening calls and a friend's affidavit show continued persecution risk even in Islamabad.

propositions.text: Pakistani police may be corrupt and leak Applicant's location, undermining IFA viability
propositions.quote: documentary evidence suggests that the Pakistani police force is inefficient, corrupt, and may be complicit with the persecuting organizations. Counsel postulated that certain members of the police force could leak the Applicant’s location to the persecutors. According to the Applicant’s counsel, the possibility of a leak undermines the possibility of an IFA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's counsel argues police corruption and possible leaks undermine the viability of the IFA.

propositions.text: RAD found persecutors had no interest in chasing Applicant to Islamabad due to closed drugstore and no contraceptive sales
propositions.quote: The RAD determined that the agents of persecution had no interest in chasing the Applicant to Islamabad since his drugstore was closed and he stopped selling contraceptives.

propositions.text: RAD noted Applicant failed to provide evidence of aggressors' ability or intent to find him in Islamabad
propositions.quote: The RAD also noted that the Applicant had failed to provide evidence as to the aggressors’ ability or intentions to find him in Islamabad .

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found no interest by persecutors in Islamabad and lack of evidence of aggressors' intent or ability to find Applicant there.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant could avoid threatening calls by changing phone number and no evidence of assailants' location or knowledge of Applicant's whereabouts in Karachi
propositions.quote: the RAD determined that the Applicant could avoid these types of calls by changing his telephone number from the one he used for his drugstore. In any event, there was no evidence as to where the assailants were calling from, or that they knew that the Applicant was in Karachi at the time of the call.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Applicant could avoid calls by changing number and no evidence assailants knew his Karachi location.

propositions.text: RAD found assailants unaware of Applicant's whereabouts and lack of threats to family shows little interest in targeting Applicant
propositions.quote: The RAD determined that the friend’s report indicating that the assailants were returning to the Applicant’s former drugstore looking for him simply shows that the aggressors were unaware of the Applicant’s whereabouts. The RAD also determined that the lack of threats directed against the Applicant’s spouse and children in Karachi or his father and siblings in Sahiwal shows that the aggressors have little interest in targeting the Applicant.

propositions.text: Mere suspicions of being hunted in home country insufficient to preclude acceptable IFA location
propositions.quote: Mere suspicions of being hunted in one’s home country is insufficient to preclude an otherwise acceptable IFA location (Kumar v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2012 FC 30 at para 35).

paragraphs.summary: RAD found assailants unaware of Applicant's location and no threats to family; mere suspicions insufficient to reject IFA location.

propositions.text: RAD ruled Applicant failed to show relocation to IFA would expose him to unacceptable risk
propositions.quote: the RAD ruled that the Applicant had not discharged his burden to show that relocation to the proposed IFA would expose him to an unacceptable risk (Gallo Farias at para 23; Thirunavukkarasu at para 12; Mwaura v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2008 FC 748 at para 13; Whenu v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2003 FC 1041 at para 11).

paragraphs.summary: RAD ruled Applicant failed to prove relocation to IFA posed unacceptable risk.

propositions.text: RAD found insufficient evidence of risk in Islamabad
propositions.quote: According to the RAD, the Applicant failed to provide sufficient evidence as to his risk of persecution in Islamabad .

propositions.text: Court finds RAD's findings on risk in Islamabad reasonable and will not disturb them
propositions.quote: I see nothing unreasonable about the RAD’s findings on this issue, and thus no reason to disturb the RAD’s determination under the first prong of the Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found insufficient evidence of risk in Islamabad; Court finds RAD's findings reasonable and will not disturb them.

propositions.text: Applicant submits RAD's second prong analysis incomplete for failing to address full range of issues
propositions.quote: the Applicant submits that the RAD’s analysis under the second prong of the Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test was incomplete because it failed to address the full range of issues in determining whether, even if the first prong was met, it was reasonable for the Applicant to seek refuge in Islamabad .

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits RAD's second prong analysis incomplete for not addressing full range of issues.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD should have addressed transportation, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status, healthcare
propositions.quote: the Applicant submits that the RAD should have addressed the full range of issues related to the IFA location, namely, transportation and travel, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status and the availability of healthcare.

propositions.text: Applicant cites RAD case lacking legal basis for enumerated factors and says RAD unjustifiably omitted these issues
propositions.quote: In support of this argument, the Applicant cites a case from the RAD, one that does not cite a legal basis for the enumerated factors. The Applicant believes that the RAD unjustifiably omitted to address these issues.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD should have addressed various factors and unjustifiably omitted them, citing a RAD case without legal basis.

propositions.text: RAD claimed Applicant did not contest RPD's second prong analysis
propositions.quote: In its decision, the RAD claimed that the Applicant did not contest the RPD’s analysis under the second prong.

propositions.text: Applicant says RAD misconstrued his appeal memorandum which challenged RPD's lack of analysis on state protection in Islamabad
propositions.quote: To the Applicant, this justification misconstrues the written argumentation in his appeal memorandum, wherein he challenges the RPD’s lack of analysis as to the sufficiency of state protection in Islamabad .

paragraphs.summary: RAD said Applicant did not contest RPD's second prong; Applicant says RAD misconstrued his memorandum challenging state protection analysis.

propositions.text: Respondent agrees RAD need not address each factor as second prong was uncontested and no evidence shows RAD's determination unreasonable
propositions.quote: The Respondent agrees with the RAD, and argues that it was unnecessary to address each factor because the second prong of the test was uncontested by the Applicant. Moreover, the Respondent argues that the Applicant has not provided any evidence that shows how the substance of the RAD’s determination was unreasonable under the second prong of the test.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent agrees RAD need not address each factor as second prong was uncontested and no evidence shows unreasonableness.

propositions.text: Court rejects Applicant's arguments for four reasons
propositions.quote: I reject the Applicant’s arguments for four reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects Applicant's arguments for four reasons.

propositions.text: Applicant did not raise 'range of issues' argument at RAD level despite burden of proof
propositions.quote: First, the Applicant’s argument regarding the ‘range of issues’ under the second prong was not raised at the RAD level. The Applicant did not raise such arguments in his memorandum at the RAD, despite the Applicant’s burden of proof to demonstrate how a proposed IFA would be unsuitable.

propositions.text: Applicant only challenged RPD's analysis on state protection, relating to first prong
propositions.quote: Indeed, the Applicant merely challenges the RPD’s analysis as to the level of state protection in Islamabad , a consideration that relates to the first prong of the Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test (i.e., the analysis pertaining to the fear of persecution).

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant did not raise 'range of issues' at RAD and only challenged RPD's state protection analysis related to first prong.

propositions.text: Applicant's RAD memorandum omits factors like transportation, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status, healthcare
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s memorandum before the RAD does not mention the factors of transportation and travel, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status and the availability of healthcare.

propositions.text: Raising new legal issues at judicial review is impermissible
propositions.quote: As a result, the Applicant is attempting to raise new legal issues that could have been raised prior to this judicial review (Alberta (Information and Privacy Commissioner) v Alberta Teachers’ Association, 2011 SCC 61 at paras 22-26; Forest Ethics Advocacy Association v Canada (National Energy Board), [2015] 4 FCR 75, 2014 FCA 245 at paras 42-47; Erasmo v Canada (Attorney General), 2015 FCA 129 at para 33).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's RAD memorandum omits key factors; court rules raising new legal issues at judicial review is impermissible.

propositions.text: Second prong's 'reasonable in all circumstances' standard is high and fact-specific, requiring concrete evidence of jeopardizing conditions
propositions.quote: The “reasonable in all the circumstances” standard (of the second prong of the Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test) is a high threshold that cannot be defined in an abstract manner. That standard requires “nothing less than the existence of conditions which would jeopardize the life and safety of a claimant in travelling or temporarily relocating to a safe area” as well as “actual and concrete evidence of such conditions.” (Ranganathan v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [2001] 2 FC 164, 2000 CanLII 16789 (FCA) at para 15, referring to Thirunavukkarasu at 597, 599).

propositions.text: Applicant's argument would improperly confine fact-sensitive inquiry and shift burden to tribunal
propositions.quote: If accepted, the Applicant’s argument would confine this fact-sensitive inquiry and transfer the burden of proof to the tribunal. These consequences would frustrate the contextual, case-by-case nature of the test.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains second prong's high, fact-specific standard and rejects Applicant's argument as improperly shifting burden to tribunal.

propositions.text: Applicant provided no evidence or substantive argument on Islamabad's adequacy for employment, shelter, transport, education, healthcare, or services
propositions.quote: The Applicant has not provided evidence or made a substantive argument as to Islamabad ’s inability to provide adequate employment, shelter, transportation, education, healthcare, and services adapted to the Applicant’s situation (e.g., language, religion, indigenous status).

propositions.text: Applicant faults RAD for not assessing IFA suitability but burden lies with Applicant
propositions.quote: Instead, the Applicant tries to fault the RAD for not taking upon itself this task. Again, the burden to show how a proposed IFA location is unsuitable lies with the Applicant – not the RAD.

propositions.text: Burden to show undue hardship in IFA location lies with Applicant (Okonkwo v Canada)
propositions.quote: It is the Applicant’s burden to show how relocation would cause him an undue hardship in the light of the Applicant’s particular situation and objective information related to the proposed IFA location (e.g., Okonkwo v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2019 FC 1330 at para 17).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant gave no evidence on Islamabad's adequacy; burden to show IFA unsuitability lies with Applicant, not RAD.

propositions.text: Court will not reweigh evidence on second prong in judicial review
propositions.quote: the Applicant is essentially asking this Court to reweigh the evidence under this second prong; that is not the role of the Court in judicial review proceedings (Vavilov at para 125; Akinfolajimi v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2018 FC 722 at paras 27-28; Titcombe at para 22; Khosa at para 61).

paragraphs.summary: Court will not reweigh evidence on second prong in judicial review proceedings.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed; no question for certification
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is dismissed. There is no question for certification.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses application for judicial review and finds no question for certification.
